images.caption: Imperial Japanese Navy warships under Vice Admiral Nobutake Kondo head for Guadalcanal to bombard Henderson Field on November 14, 1942.  Photographed from heavy cruiser Atago.  Battlecruiser Kirishima (background) is preceded in formation by heavy cruiser Takao (center).  Kirishima was sunk in battle by the United States Navy battleship USS Washington hours after this photo was taken.
images.alt: Imperial Japanese Navy warships under Vice Admiral Nobutake Kondo head for Guadalcanal to bombard Henderson Field on November 14, 1942.  Photographed from heavy cruiser Atago.  Battlecruiser Kirishima (background) is preceded in formation by heavy cruiser Takao (center).  Kirishima was sunk in battle by the United States Navy battleship USS Washington hours after this photo was taken.

images.filename: Japanese Center Force ships leave Brunei Bay, Borneo, on 22 October 1944 (NH 63435).jpg
images.caption: Battle of Leyte Gulf, October 1944: The Japanese "Center Force" leaves Brunei Bay, Borneo, on 22 October 1944, en route to the Philippines. Ships are, from right to left: battleships Nagato, Musashi and Yamato; heavy cruisers Maya, Chōkai, Takao, Atago, Haguro and Myōkō.
images.alt: Battle of Leyte Gulf, October 1944: The Japanese "Center Force" leaves Brunei Bay, Borneo, on 22 October 1944, en route to the Philippines. Ships are, from right to left: battleships Nagato, Musashi and Yamato; heavy cruisers Maya, Chōkai, Takao, Atago, Haguro and Myōkō.

images.caption: A view of the Japanese fleet anchored in Staring Bay taken from the floatplane of the heavy cruiser Atago. Several Japanese ships are labeled, including the aircraft carriers Akagi and Kaga, the battleships Kongo, Hiei, and Kirishima, the heavy cruisers Takao, Atago, Tone, and Chikuma, and the light cruiser Abukuma. The four destroyers of desdiv 17 (Urakaze, Isokaze, Tanikaze, and Hamakaze) are seen anchored ahead of Abukuma, as are several support ships.
images.alt: A view of the Japanese fleet anchored in Staring Bay taken from the floatplane of the heavy cruiser Atago. Several Japanese ships are labeled, including the aircraft carriers Akagi and Kaga, the battleships Kongo, Hiei, and Kirishima, the heavy cruisers Takao, Atago, Tone, and Chikuma, and the light cruiser Abukuma. The four destroyers of desdiv 17 (Urakaze, Isokaze, Tanikaze, and Hamakaze) are seen anchored ahead of Abukuma, as are several support ships.

images.caption: A view taken from the stern of the Japanese heavy cruiser Atago shortly after the start of the Pacific War of the Japanese fleet arriving at Camranh Bay, Indochina.
